blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 17 (Human Reproductive System), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 Which function belongs to the female reproductive system but not the male?

options.text: Nourishing the fertilized egg cell and providing an environment for its development
Delivering gametes to the other sex

blocks.explanation: Both systems make and prepare gametes; the male delivers gametes, the female nourishes the fertilized egg and provides an environment for its development.

book_ref.quote: the female reproductive system nourishes the fertilized egg cell

blocks.prompt: 2 Unlike other body systems, the reproductive system becomes functional:
blocks.explanation: Other systems are functional since or shortly after birth; the reproductive system becomes functional only at puberty.

book_ref.quote: The reproductive system does not become functional until at puberty

blocks.prompt: 3 The testes are located in a skin pouch called the:
blocks.explanation: Two testes lie outside the abdomen in a skin pouch called the scrotum.

book_ref.quote: Two testes are located outside the abdomen in a skin pouch called scrotum

blocks.prompt: 4 Each human testis measures about:
blocks.explanation: Each oval testis is about 3–5 cm long and 2–3 cm wide.

book_ref.quote: measures about 3–5 cm in length and 2–3 cm in width

blocks.prompt: 5 In the germinal epithelium, the developing sperms are nourished by:
blocks.explanation: The germinal epithelium has germline cells (make sperms by meiosis) and Sertoli cells (nourish developing sperms).

book_ref.quote: Sertoli cell nourish the developing sperms

blocks.prompt: 6 The scrotum keeps the testes at a temperature of about:
blocks.explanation: The scrotum keeps the testes at about 34°C, slightly lower than core body temperature (37°C); this is required for sperm development.

book_ref.quote: The scrotum maintains the testes at around 34°C

blocks.prompt: 7 During development the testes form within the abdominal cavity and descend into the scrotum:

options.text: at about 10 to 14 years of age

blocks.explanation: The testes form in the abdominal cavity and descend into the scrotum shortly before birth.

book_ref.quote: Shortly before birth, they descend through an opening into the scrotum

blocks.prompt: 8 From the seminiferous tubules, spermatozoa first enter a network of tubules called the:
blocks.explanation: From the seminiferous tubules sperms enter the rete testis, then the epididymis.

book_ref.quote: the spermatozoa enter into a network of tubules called rete testis

blocks.prompt: 9 Spermatozoa remain in the epididymis for at least:
blocks.explanation: Sperms are non-motile on entering the epididymis; they stay there at least 18 hours and then become motile.

book_ref.quote: They remain in epididymis for at least 18 hours

blocks.prompt: 10 The vas deferens passes into the abdominal cavity through the:
blocks.explanation: The vas deferens passes into the abdominal cavity via the inguinal canal.

book_ref.quote: passes into the abdominal cavity via the inguinal canal

blocks.prompt: 11 The tube formed by the joining of the vas deferens and the duct of a seminal vesicle is the:
blocks.explanation: After joining the seminal vesicle duct, the vas deferens is called the ejaculatory duct; both ejaculatory ducts pass through the prostate into the urethra.

book_ref.quote: After joining, the tube is called the ejaculatory duct

blocks.prompt: 12 The soft and spongy male accessory gland lying just below the urinary bladder is the:
blocks.explanation: The prostate gland lies just below the urinary bladder and is soft and spongy.

book_ref.quote: The prostate gland lies just below the urinary bladder

blocks.prompt: 13 Semen is a mixture of sperms and fluids from the:
blocks.explanation: Semen is a mixture of sperms and fluids from the seminal vesicles and the prostate gland.

book_ref.quote: Semen is a mixture of sperms and fluids from the seminal vesicles and the prostate gland

blocks.prompt: 14 The clear fluid that lubricates the urethra and provides a protective neutral environment for sperms comes from the:
blocks.explanation: The two small bulbourethral glands secrete a clear fluid that lubricates the urethra and gives a neutral environment.

book_ref.quote: provides a protective neutral environment for sperms to survive

blocks.prompt: 15 The male copulatory organ (penis) contains:

options.text: urethra, erectile tissue, an artery and two veins

blocks.explanation: The penis contains the urethra, erectile tissue, an artery and two veins.

book_ref.quote: It contains urethra, erectile tissue, an artery and two veins

blocks.prompt: 16 In the walls of the seminiferous tubules, germline cells (2n) divide by mitosis to form:
blocks.explanation: Germline cells divide by mitosis; some new cells become spermatogonia (2n), others remain germline cells for future use.

book_ref.quote: Some of the new cells become spermatogonia (2n)

blocks.prompt: 17 Primary spermatocytes are:

options.text: diploid (2n) and move toward the lumen of the tubules
haploid and mature directly into sperms
diploid and remain in the epididymis

blocks.explanation: Spermatogonia form primary spermatocytes (2n), which move toward the lumen and divide by meiosis-I.

book_ref.quote: Primary spermatocytes move toward the inner space (lumen) of the tubules

blocks.prompt: 18 One spermatogonium (2n) finally produces:

options.text: one spermatid and three polar bodies

blocks.explanation: Primary spermatocyte → 2 secondary spermatocytes (meiosis-I) → 4 spermatids (meiosis-II).

book_ref.quote: one spermatogonium (2n) produces four spermatids (1n)

blocks.prompt: 19 The thick cap surrounding about two-thirds of the sperm head is the:
blocks.explanation: The acrosome covers about two-thirds of the head; it is formed mainly of Golgi body and contains enzymes for fertilization.

book_ref.quote: About two-thirds of the head is surrounded by a thick cap called the acrosome

blocks.prompt: 20 The acrosome of a sperm is formed mainly from the:
blocks.explanation: The acrosome is formed mainly of Golgi body.

book_ref.quote: The acrosome is formed mainly of Golgi Body

blocks.prompt: 21 The midpiece of a sperm contains:
blocks.explanation: The midpiece has mitochondria and a centriole; the genetic material is in the head.

book_ref.quote: The midpiece contains mitochondria and a centriole

blocks.prompt: 22 The tail of a sperm is formed of microtubules (axial filament) arising from the:
blocks.explanation: The tail's microtubules (axial filament) arise from the centriole of the midpiece.

book_ref.quote: The tail is formed of microtubules (axial filament)

blocks.prompt: 23 Non-motile spermatozoa move from the lumen of seminiferous tubules into the epididymis with the help of:
blocks.explanation: Mature sperms in the lumen are non-motile; fluid secreted by Sertoli cells carries them into the epididymis, where they gain motility.

book_ref.quote: They enter the epididymis with the help of the fluid secreted by Sertoli cells

blocks.prompt: 24 The hormone released by the hypothalamus that stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH is:
blocks.explanation: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), which stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH.

book_ref.quote: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)

blocks.prompt: 25 Leydig cells are located in the:

options.text: interstitial tissue between the seminiferous tubules

blocks.explanation: LH stimulates Leydig cells, located in the interstitial tissue between the seminiferous tubules.

book_ref.quote: located in the interstitial tissue between the seminiferous tubules

blocks.prompt: 26 Inhibin, which inhibits further FSH secretion, is released by:
blocks.explanation: FSH causes the Sertoli cells to release the peptide hormone inhibin, which inhibits further FSH secretion.

book_ref.quote: it causes the Sertoli cells to release a peptide hormone called inhibin

blocks.prompt: 27 A rise in testosterone level inhibits the release of:
blocks.explanation: Testosterone (secreted under LH) inhibits the release of LH and GnRH: negative feedback.

book_ref.quote: the release of testosterone inhibits the release of LH and GnRH

blocks.prompt: 28 Which is a function of testosterone?
blocks.explanation: Testosterone stimulates the development of germinal epithelium and maintains male secondary sexual characteristics.

book_ref.quote: Testosterone stimulates the development of germinal epithelium

blocks.prompt: 29 The accessory organs of the female reproductive system are:
blocks.explanation: The female system has gonads, oviducts, uterus and vagina; the last three are accessory organs.

book_ref.quote: The oviducts, uterus and vagina are called accessory organs

blocks.prompt: 30 The functional units of the ovary are the:
blocks.explanation: The ovary contains many tiny sac-like ovarian follicles, its functional units, which nurture immature eggs.

book_ref.quote: ovarian follicles which are the functional units of ovary

blocks.prompt: 31 After ovulation, the ruptured follicle is transformed into the:
blocks.explanation: After ovulation the ruptured follicle becomes a glandular structure called the corpus luteum.

book_ref.quote: the ruptured follicle is transformed into a glandular structure called the corpus luteum

blocks.prompt: 32 The ovum travels along the oviduct toward the uterus with the help of:

options.text: cilia on the inner lining of the oviduct

blocks.explanation: The ovum's movement toward the uterus is facilitated by cilia on the inner lining of the oviduct.

book_ref.quote: This movement is facilitated by the movements of cilia on the inner lining of oviduct

blocks.prompt: 33 The zygote begins several mitotic divisions while it is still in the:
blocks.explanation: Fertilization occurs in the oviduct and the zygote undergoes several mitotic divisions while still there.

book_ref.quote: The resulting zygote undergoes several mitotic divisions while still in oviduct

blocks.prompt: 34 The uppermost rounded part of the uterus above the openings of the oviducts is the:
blocks.explanation: The uterus has three parts: fundus (uppermost, above oviduct openings), body (major portion) and cervix (lower narrow part).

book_ref.quote: Fundus is the uppermost rounded portion above the openings of oviducts

blocks.prompt: 35 The lower narrow part of the uterus that opens into the vagina is the:
blocks.explanation: The lower narrow part of the uterus is the cervix; its opening leads to the vagina.

book_ref.quote: The lower narrow part of uterus is called cervix

blocks.prompt: 36 The middle thick layer of the uterine wall, made of smooth muscles, is the:
blocks.explanation: Uterine wall: perimetrium (outer thin), myometrium (middle thick smooth muscle), endometrium (inner spongy lining).

book_ref.quote: The myometrium is the middle thick layer composed of smooth muscles

blocks.prompt: 37 The functional layer of the endometrium is regenerated by stem cells of the:
blocks.explanation: The endometrium has a basal layer, whose stem cells regenerate the functional layer that is shed in each cycle.

book_ref.quote: The basal layer has the stems cells which regenerate the functional layer

blocks.prompt: 38 During pregnancy, the vascular spaces of the functional layer of the endometrium fuse to form the:
blocks.explanation: The functional layer thickens further for implantation; its vascular spaces fuse to form the placenta, which supplies oxygen and nutrition to the embryo and foetus.

book_ref.quote: forming the placenta, which supplies oxygen and nutrition to the embryo and foetus

blocks.prompt: 39 The vagina is a thin-walled tube about:
blocks.explanation: The vagina is a thin-walled 8-10 cm tube from outside to the cervix; it is the passage for delivery and menstrual flow.

book_ref.quote: It is a thin-walled 8-10 cm long tube

blocks.prompt: 40 During embryonic development of a female, primary oocytes begin meiosis-I but stop in:
blocks.explanation: Oogonia (2n) divide by mitosis to form primary oocytes (2n), which begin meiosis-I and stop in prophase-I through childhood.

book_ref.quote: These primary oocytes begin the first meiotic division, but stop in prophase-I

blocks.prompt: 41 The secondary oocyte stops its division at:
blocks.explanation: After meiosis-I at puberty, the secondary oocyte stops division in metaphase-II until a sperm fuses with it.

book_ref.quote: The secondary oocyte stops division in metaphase-II

blocks.prompt: 42 Meiosis-I of a primary oocyte produces:

options.text: an ovum and a second polar body
a large secondary oocyte and a small first polar body

blocks.explanation: Meiosis-I gives two dissimilar haploid cells: the larger secondary oocyte (1n) and the smaller first polar body (1n).

book_ref.quote: The larger cell is the secondary oocyte (1n) while smaller one is called the first polar body (1n)

blocks.prompt: 43 When a sperm fuses with the secondary oocyte, meiosis-II is completed and produces:

options.text: one large ovum and a small second polar body

blocks.explanation: On fusion with a sperm the secondary oocyte quickly completes meiosis-II in the oviduct, giving one large ovum (1n) and a small second polar body (1n).

book_ref.quote: It produces two new cells i.e., one large ovum (1n) and a small second polar body (1n)

blocks.prompt: 44 If an ovulated secondary oocyte is not fertilized by a sperm, it:
blocks.explanation: An ovulated secondary oocyte that is not fertilized dies.

book_ref.quote: If an ovulated secondary oocyte is not fertilized by a sperm, it dies

blocks.prompt: 45 At birth, a female's ovaries contain about:
blocks.explanation: At birth the ovaries contain some 2 million follicles, each with a primary oocyte.

book_ref.quote: At birth, a female’s ovaries contain some 2 million follicles

blocks.text: Female Reproductive Cycle - The Menstrual Cycle

blocks.prompt: 46 On average, the menstrual cycle lasts:
blocks.explanation: The menstrual cycle lasts approximately one month, 28 days on average.

book_ref.quote: The menstrual cycle lasts approximately one month (28 days on average)

blocks.prompt: 47 Menstruation (shedding of the functional layer of endometrium) occurs due to:

options.text: high levels of estrogen and progesterone
low levels of estrogen and progesterone

blocks.explanation: Menstruation, lasting 3-5 days, occurs due to low levels of estrogen and progesterone.

book_ref.quote: It occurs due to low levels of estrogen and progesterone hormones

blocks.prompt: 48 When FSH rises at the start of the proliferative phase:

options.text: all follicles mature and release eggs
a few follicles start growing, but only one grows fully and the others degenerate

blocks.explanation: A few follicles grow; only one becomes the mature Graafian follicle and the rest degenerate.

book_ref.quote: But, only one follicle grows full and the others degenerate

blocks.prompt: 49 In the proliferative phase, estrogen from the Graafian follicle:

options.text: makes the endometrium vascular, velvety and thick again

blocks.explanation: Estrogen causes initial vascularization of the endometrium and makes it velvety and thick again.

book_ref.quote: It causes the initial vascularization of endometrium and makes it velvety and thick again

blocks.prompt: 50 In the proliferative phase, the level of FSH falls because of:

options.text: release of inhibin from Leydig cells

blocks.explanation: As estrogen concentration rises, FSH falls due to negative feedback.

book_ref.quote: As the concentration of estrogen rises, the level of FSH falls due to negative feedback

blocks.prompt: 51 The colour of the corpus luteum is:
blocks.explanation: After ovulation, LH makes the ruptured Graafian follicle develop into a yellow structure, the corpus luteum.

book_ref.quote: develop into a yellow structure called the corpus luteum

blocks.prompt: 52 If fertilization does not occur, the abrupt fall in estrogen and progesterone results from:

options.text: growth of a new Graafian follicle

blocks.explanation: Without fertilization the corpus luteum degenerates; this causes an abrupt fall in estrogen and progesterone and menstruation on day 28.

book_ref.quote: the corpus luteum starts to degenerate

blocks.prompt: 53 After fertilization, the corpus luteum is maintained by:
blocks.explanation: The tiny embryo secretes human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), which maintains the corpus luteum, so menstruation is prevented.

book_ref.quote: the tiny embryo secretes human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)

blocks.prompt: 54 The hormone tested for in all pregnancy tests is:
blocks.explanation: hCG comes from the embryonic chorion, not the mother, so it is tested for in all pregnancy tests.

book_ref.quote: it is the hormone that is tested for in all pregnancy tests

blocks.prompt: 55 The stopping of the menstrual cycle at around 50 years of age is called:
blocks.explanation: In human females the menstrual cycle stops around 50 years of age; this is menopause.

book_ref.quote: menstrual cycle stops around 50 year of age and it is termed as menopause
